transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-11
Time: 15:00 UTC (7:00 PT)
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Ava Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Lena Ortiz (Galeview Head of Search), Tom Briggs (Galeview ML Eng), Rajiv Das (Galeview CTO)

Summary:
Quick hosted API demo focused on embeddings + two-stage rerank flow, with emphasis on query-rewrite opportunity and pilot next steps. Discussed security requirements (SOC2, SSO), latency/cost tradeoffs, and pilot scope (100k docs). Redwood to provide benchmark and pricing.

Topics:
- Galeview current stack and pain points
- Two-stage retrieval: ann indexing vs candidate gen + rerank
- Query rewrite candidates and prefix caching
- Hosted embeddings endpoint and reranker endpoint demo
- Pilot scope and security/compliance checklist

Action items (recap at end): Ava to send pricing & docs; Samir to run benchmark; Tom to provide data.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ava Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining uh we'll kick off in a sec, appreciate you carving time. i'm ava from Redwood, on the AE side, and with me is samir our solutions engineer.
[00:18] Lena Ortiz: hi ava, hi samir, thanks. i'm lena, i run search at galeview. happy to dig in, we've got tom and rajiv on too.
[00:26] Tom Briggs: hey all, quick context — we're refreshing our search infra, aiming to improve relevance for long-tail product queries and cut down our query-to-click latency.
[00:36] Samir Patel: great, thanks tom. quick agenda — we'll run through the hosted embeddings + rerank flow in the console, show how query rewrite could slot in, then discuss pilot sizing and security. does that align?
[00:46] Rajiv Das: yes, sounds good. curious about latency overhead for reranking and cost delta.
[00:52] Ava Martinez: noted — we'll show numbers and how batching/caching affects it.
[01:05] Ava Martinez: to start, can you share your current stack real quick — what are you using for vector search and any reranker today?
[01:15] Lena Ortiz: currently we index embeddings in a managed vector DB, using a sparse retrieval first (like bm25) then a lightweight cross-encoder for top 20. but the cross-encoder is slow and expensive at scale. we also do some ad-hoc query rewrite rules.
[01:30] Samir Patel: totally — that's very common. the two-stage approach is exactly where Redwood's hosted embeddings + rerank can help: hosted emb endpoint for offload, then our reranker (cross-encoder style) as a separate endpoint that runs only on candidates so you reduce unit cost.
[01:45] Tom Briggs: how do you handle candidate generation? do you support mixing BM25 and vector ANN?
[01:52] Samir Patel: yes, you can combine sources — we often recommend hybrid recall: BM25 (or your current ANN) for recall, then run our reranker on top N. You can implement it client-side or route through our pipeline via the Redwood Console routing if you'd like managed flow.
[02:10] Lena Ortiz: one pain point — we get very noisy short queries from customers, e.g., "cheap battery for model X" — rewrite could help normalize that. can redwood do rewrite suggestions?
[02:20] Samir Patel: good question — Redwood Optimize includes query rewrite suggestions and prompt sets that pair well with embeddings. For the hosted pilot we can include a small rewrite step — either service-side in the pipeline or run rewrite client-side using a lightweight LLM call. the benefit is higher recall into the embedding match set.
[02:36] Rajiv Das: what's the typical latency for the reranker if i send top 50 candidates?
[02:41] Samir Patel: typical numbers — on hosted, a cross-encoder rerank for 50 candidates averages around 120-250ms per request depending on model selection and batching. if you need sub-100ms at low concurrency we can discuss model distillation or limit to top 20. also you can use quantized model variants to cut cost.
[03:00] Tom Briggs: 120-250ms is ok sometimes, but at 200ms median it's adding up. what's the cost impact?
[03:08] Ava Martinez: cost depends on tokens processed in rerank and model family. for a hosted pilot with our recommended mid-tier cross-encoder model, we usually estimate X dollars per 100k queries — we'll send exact numbers in the pricing doc. important levers are batch window, top-k, and using a lighter cross-encoder for re-rank.
[03:25] Lena Ortiz: can you show the console demo — embeddings endpoint and rerank flow?
[03:30] Samir Patel: absolutely — i'm going to share my screen.
[03:36] [Screen share noise — short pause]
[03:44] Samir Patel: okay this is the Redwood Console, nav to Models -> Hosted -> Embeddings. you can create an embeddings key and see usage. i'll run a quick sample embedding call against a query and then show the rerank endpoint invoking a cross-encoder on the candidates.
[03:59] [typing sounds]
[04:06] Samir Patel: sending a sample request now — here's the simple REST call, it's a one-line payload: {"input":"cheap battery model X"} and we get back an embedding vector. transcription note: actual JSON shown in console.
[04:22] Tom Briggs: okay got it. latency on that single embedding call?
[04:26] Samir Patel: usually ~20-35ms for a short input, because embeddings are optimized in the runtime for small token payloads. larger queries or full documents will be higher.
[04:36] Lena Ortiz: then you pass the vectors into our ANN — can redwood host the ANN or do we keep ours?
[04:42] Samir Patel: Redwood doesn't replace your ANN — we integrate. you can keep your vector DB (Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenSearch etc.) and use our embeddings. alternatively, we can host vector nearest-neighbor as part of a managed workflow for pilots if you'd like a single-hosted flow.
[04:58] Rajiv Das: say we want to keep our current ann but want hosted rerank — what's the easiest integration path?
[05:05] Samir Patel: simplest: your app performs recall against your ANN, returns top N candidate IDs + metadata; you call Redwood rerank endpoint with the original query and candidate texts or embeddings, and we return reranked IDs and scores. This minimizes data movement and keeps control in your app.
[05:22] Tom Briggs: do you accept embeddings from our DB to avoid re-sending documents?
[05:27] Samir Patel: yes we accept either raw text or embeddings. if you send embeddings, the reranker can directly operate on them which saves tokenization and speeds things up. small caveat: cross-encoders still need textual context for best accuracy in some configurations, but we support mixed inputs.
[05:45] Lena Ortiz: earlier you mentioned prefix/KV cache — can you explain how that helps latency?
[05:50] Samir Patel: sure — Redwood runtime does KV cache for decoder models and prefix caching for repeated prompts; for rerank specifically, if queries share common prefixes or templates after rewrite, we can reuse pre-computed encodings and reduce compute. Also, we have automatic batching where micro-batches combine requests when safe for your SLO.
[06:10] Rajiv Das: security — we need SOC2 and SSO, plus audit logs and data residency in the EU. do you support that on hosted?
[06:18] Ava Martinez: yes — Redwood hosted is SOC2 compliant, we have SSO/SAML options, RBAC, and audit logs. for EU residency we offer region controls; if you need strict on-prem or VPC, Redwood Private is the product to look at. we'll attach the security pack with specifics.
[06:36] Tom Briggs: for the pilot we prefer hosted with EU region + encrypted at rest, but not full on-prem yet.
[06:42] Ava Martinez: that's common and fully supported. we'll include region configuration and KMS docs in the pack.
[06:50] Samir Patel: i'm going to demo a quick rerank call now — using the reranker endpoint, i'll pass the user query and 10 candidate snippets in the payload.
[06:58] [typing]
[07:06] Samir Patel: request payload here, note — shorter candidate snippets yields faster token processing. sending now...
[07:15] [network beep]
[07:20] Samir Patel: response back — reranked list with scores. you can see the top item moved from candidate 7 to candidate 1. notice the score margins — we provide per-candidate logits so you can tune thresholding.
[07:36] Lena Ortiz: looks clean. do you provide confidence calibration or NDCG evaluation hooks?
[07:42] Samir Patel: yes — Redwood Optimize includes built-in evals tied to prompt sets: you can run NDCG, MRR, precision@k over your labeled set and we surface regressions on rollouts. For pilots we typically run baseline vs Redwood rerank and provide a small report.
[08:00] Tom Briggs: for cost modeling, can you provide a simple formula? tokens processed in rerank x model rate + embedding calls?
[08:07] Ava Martinez: exactly. we'll include a cost calculator spreadsheet. high level: cost = embeddings_calls*embedding_unit + rerank_calls*(token_cost + model_multiplier). We'll break out examples for top-10 vs top-50.
[08:24] Rajiv Das: on data retention — we can't have logs persist for more than 90 days and a strict no PII policy.
[08:31] Ava Martinez: we support configurable retention windows and scrub policies. for PII you can use client-side tokenization or redact before sending. also Redwood Private/full VPC allows you to keep data inside your network.
[08:45] Lena Ortiz: could you show the routing rules in the Console for a canary rollout? we want to test 10% traffic to rerank A vs B.
[08:52] Samir Patel: yep — Console -> Routes. you can define a rule: 10% traffic to model variant A (e.g., quantized model), 90% to baseline. we also support automatic rollback if quality metrics drop below threshold.
[09:10] Tom Briggs: what's the friction to change models if performance regresses in production?
[09:14] Samir Patel: low — you can pin model versions and do canary or A/B. if latency spikes we can fallback to a cheaper model or to baseline BM25 recall only, preserving availability.
[09:28] [brief pause]
[09:35] Samir Patel: i want to call out a pattern that helped a similar customer: run ANN retrieval for top 200, use a light-weight embed similarity to filter to 50, then rerank top 20 with a cross-encoder. that reduces token and computation cost while improving NDCG.
[09:50] Lena Ortiz: can you walk us through the pilot proposal — what's included?
[09:55] Ava Martinez: pilot scope we propose: 4-week hosted pilot, up to 100k documents, up to 1000 queries/day synthetic load for benchmarking. deliverables: benchmark report (latency/cost/NDCG), tuning suggestions, a small integration guide, and a playbook for rollout. price and SOW we'll include.
[10:12] Rajiv Das: 4-weeks seems reasonable. do you need any VPN or special network setup?
[10:16] Samir Patel: for hosted no. If you want S3 data upload we can pull from a pre-signed S3 link. for VPC/private we'd need config.
[10:24] Tom Briggs: what's the expected CPU/GPU resource for the reranker in hosted? we plan to budget infra costs tightly.
[10:30] Samir Patel: hosted is billed per inference units — under the hood we use GPU-optimized runtime and kernel selection. for cross-encoder mid-tier model, it's typically 0.2-0.5 GPU-seconds per 10 requests depending on batching. we'll put concrete numbers in the benchmark.
[10:48] Lena Ortiz: i saw reference in docs to "prefix caching" — any chance that helps reuse across similar conversions?
[10:55] Samir Patel: yes, if your queries share structure after rewrite we can cache encoded prefixes to skip repeated work. this is more effective with templated queries.
[11:06] Tom Briggs: how do you instrument the end-to-end to show token/cost breakdown?
[11:11] Ava Martinez: Redwood Console provides token-level breakdown per request, plus per-model cost. you can filter by route, user token, or timeframe. we also surface traces for slow requests.
[11:25] Rajiv Das: competitors — do you integrate with Pinecone natively?
[11:29] Samir Patel: yes we have integration plugins and example code for Pinecone, Weaviate, OpenSearch. we'll send sample connectors.
[11:36] Lena Ortiz: any gotchas with aggregating labeled data for evals? we have sporadic labels in our ticketing system.
[11:42] Samir Patel: that's common — we recommend a small curated dev set of 1k-5k queries with labels for NDCG; we can help extract and format labels. we also support periodic sampling and human-in-the-loop labeling through integrations.
[11:58] Tom Briggs: let's talk data transfer — for 100k docs how long to upload and index?
[12:03] Samir Patel: depends on doc size; for 100k short docs it's typically a few hours if you upload a compressed S3 export. indexing in your ANN varies; Redwood's managed indexing pipeline can help parallelize if desired.
[12:18] Ava Martinez: quick demo note — i'll attach the console walkthrough recording after the call plus links to docs.
[12:25] [screen share stop]
[12:30] Lena Ortiz: good, thanks. a few questions from tom — do you support partial reranks (only reordering existing top 10) vs full scoring?
[12:40] Samir Patel: yes, you can choose to only re-score and re-order top N without computing new candidates. it's configurable.
[12:48] Tom Briggs: tuning — how do you avoid certified regressions when swapping models?
[12:52] Samir Patel: Redwood Optimize's eval pipeline runs regression tests on your labeled set; you can set alert thresholds and block rollouts automatically.
[13:04] Rajiv Das: any SLA numbers we should know for hosted?
[13:07] Ava Martinez: hosted has a baseline SLA for availability and per-model latency SLOs for paid tiers; exact numbers depend on contract level — we'll include the SLA options in the docs.
[13:20] Lena Ortiz: ok let's recap next steps.
[13:23] Ava Martinez: recap: we'll run a 1k-query rerank benchmark on a subset, we'll prototype the hosted rerank path with your ANN, and provide a pilot SOW and pricing. samir will run the bench and ava will share docs.
[13:36] Tom Briggs: i'll upload the dataset and sample queries by monday (2026-12-13).
[13:42] Rajiv Das: i'll review the security pack and confirm region + retention settings.
[13:47] Ava Martinez: perfect — final question: is there any blocker from your side to start the pilot?
[13:52] Lena Ortiz: none — timeline looks good, just want the security pack and cost numbers.
[13:58] Ava Martinez: great, we'll send the pack and pricing. thanks all, we'll follow up with calendar invites for the kick-off.
[14:06] [end of recording — small wrap-up chatter, email addresses exchanged]
